page: Amazon Web Services g6f.large is a fractional GPU accelerated virtual machine instance based on the AWS Nitro System. The server is provisioned with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core of an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. System memory consists of 8.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB per physical core. Accelerated processing is provided by a fractional partition of an NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU, representing 0.125 of a full unit with 3 GB of allocated VRAM. Direct-attached local storage is included via a 100 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is anchored at a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a profile constrained by minimal core counts and fractional GPU slicing. The AMD EPYC processor registers strong single-core compute in stress-ng at 2870.48, placing in the top quartile, but multi-core throughput sits in the lowest quartile at 2870.48 due to having only one dual-threaded physical core. Geekbench scores reflect this limitation, returning 1170.0 for single-core and 1179.0 for multi-core. Memory bandwidth tests reveal weak throughput across read and write operations, recording 20.45 GB/sec on large block reads and 18.08 GB/sec on large block writes. For accelerated workloads, the partitioned L4 GPU yields 1089.99 tokens per second for small 135M model prompt processing and 69.08 tokens per second on medium 7B model prompt processing, while text generation reaches 43.54 tokens per second on small models.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, g6f.large provides an entry tier for workloads requiring dedicated hardware acceleration without incurring the expenditure of a whole GPU. The trade-off lies in the small 3 GB VRAM ceiling and limited multi-threaded host CPU capacity, which precludes medium to large model execution or intensive parallel data preprocessing. The instance is suited for lightweight graphics processing, small model inference pipelines, entry-level video transcoding, and fractional GPU application development.
description: Amazon Web Services g6f.large is a fractional GPU accelerated instance featuring 2 vCPUs from a single AMD EPYC 7R13 core operating at 3.4 GHz, 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a 100 GB local NVMe SSD. Hardware acceleration is provided by a 0.125 fraction of an NVIDIA L4 GPU equipped with 3 GB of VRAM. Compute tests show strong single-core execution alongside weak multi-core throughput due to the single physical core layout. Memory bandwidth is bounded, registering 20.45 GB/sec on large block uncached reads. AI inference benchmarks show prompt evaluation throughput of 1089.99 tokens per second on small 135M parameter models and 69.08 tokens per second on 7B models, though generation throughput remains modest. The instance is suited for lightweight AI inference, basic graphics streaming, and low-scale development workflows needing minor GPU acceleration.
